intro: Rowing races are a test of power, endurance and perfect synchronisation. Crews of one, two, four or eight sit facing backwards and race side by side over 2,000 metres. In sculling, each rower uses two oars; in sweep rowing, each rower uses one. Eights are steered by a coxswain who calls the race. World Rowing publishes the Rules of Racing.
inThirtySeconds: Standard races are 2,000 m in straight lanes.
Sculling: two oars per rower. Sweep: one oar each.
First bow ball across the line wins.
False starts and leaving your lane are penalised.
objective: Cross the finish line first, with the boat's bow ahead of every other crew.

facts.players: Crews of 1, 2, 4 or 8 (eights include a coxswain)
facts.environment: Still water: lakes, rivers and purpose-built courses

scoring.label: Place
scoring.detail: Order of the bow crossing the finish line, judged by photo finish.

bodies.name: World Rowing
bodies.scope: International federation; publishes the Rules of Racing

rules.title: Sculling and sweep
rules.summary: Sculling boats (single, double, quad) give each rower two oars. Sweep boats (pair, four, eight) give each rower one.
rules.body: Boat classes are written in short form: 1x (single scull), 2x (double), 4x (quad), 2- (pair without coxswain), 4- (four), 8+ (eight with coxswain). Lightweight events add weight limits for rowers.

rules.title: The coxswain
rules.summary: In coxed boats, the coxswain steers, calls the stroke rate and motivates the crew.
rules.body: Coxswains face forward and must meet a minimum weight, carrying extra weight if they are too light.

rules.title: The start
rules.summary: Boats are held at the start pontoons; a crew that moves before the signal makes a false start.
rules.body: Under current rules, a false start can lead to exclusion from the race. Starts are aligned so every boat's bow is level.

rules.title: Stay in your lane
rules.summary: Crews must stay in their lane; leaving it and interfering with another crew can lead to exclusion.
rules.body: Buoy lines mark the lanes on international courses. An umpire follows each race in a motorboat.

rules.title: The finish
rules.summary: A crew finishes when its bow reaches the finish line; positions are decided by photo finish.
rules.body: A crew may finish even if a rower has lost an oar or caught a 'crab' (the oar getting stuck in the water), as long as the crew is complete.

fouls.name: Lane infringement
fouls.description: Leaving your lane and impeding a rival.

fouls.name: Underweight coxswain
fouls.description: Coxswain below the minimum weight without ballast.

flow.title: Repechage
flow.description: A second chance for crews that missed out.

flow.title: Semi-finals
flow.description: Crews race for places in the finals.

flow.title: Final A
flow.description: Six crews race for the medals.

positions.name: Stroke
positions.role: Sets the rhythm for the crew.

positions.name: Bow
positions.role: Rower nearest the front of the boat.

positions.name: Engine room
positions.role: The powerful middle seats of a four or eight.

When an oar gets caught in the water, stopping the rower.
